summary: Task 5 implementation cleanly satisfies all listed acceptance criteria. Constructor wiring for TelegramSender is correct and positional (placed adjacent to TelegramApiClient as the task hints suggested); both new constants (EVENT_BOT_TEST_MESSAGE_SENT, TEST_MESSAGE_BODY) carry the exact spec strings including the U+2705 emoji; sendTestMessage branches on bot.getOwnerChatId() with the verbatim 422 stub preserved on the null branch and the new sender call + bot_test_message_sent audit on success; failure path correctly suppresses the audit (no double-write with sender's telegram_send_failed); BotController.java is unchanged; the metadata helper produces exactly the {projectId, telegramBotId, chatId, messageId} shape; BotServiceTest is split into the three documented cases with a TelegramSender @Mock; BotControllerIT adds seedConnectedBotWithRealEncryption using real AES-GCM ciphertext and a positive-path test that asserts 200 OK + event metadata. Findings are nits only — no blockers, no high or medium issues.

findings.issue: Test duplicates the TEST_MESSAGE_BODY literal as a private constant in BotServiceTest instead of referencing BotService.TEST_MESSAGE_BODY (package-private, accessible from the same package). This introduces a drift risk: a future change to BotService.TEST_MESSAGE_BODY could be made consistent with a stale test constant and pass falsely.
findings.suggestion: Replace the test's private TEST_MESSAGE_BODY with a reference to BotService.TEST_MESSAGE_BODY so the constant has a single source of truth. Same for the OWNER_CHAT_ID literal duplication is unavoidable since it's test-only, but the body string is production-shared.

findings.issue: Inconsistent visibility on adjacent constants: EVENT_BOT_TEST_MESSAGE_SENT is private (matching its siblings EVENT_BOT_CONNECTED / EVENT_BOT_DISCONNECTED), but TEST_MESSAGE_BODY is package-private. There is no current test that references TEST_MESSAGE_BODY via this visibility — both BotServiceTest and BotControllerIT redefine or skip the literal — so the elevated visibility is unused.
findings.suggestion: Either make TEST_MESSAGE_BODY private to match the event-constant style, or make the BotServiceTest reference it directly (see prior nit) so the package-private visibility is justified.

findings.issue: Tautological assertion: assertThat(seeded.getOwnerChatId()).isEqualTo(ownerChatId) checks an in-memory value the test itself just passed into the seed helper. It does not verify the persisted Mongo document round-tripped correctly.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the line (the awaitEvent + metadata containsEntry on chatId already prove the ownerChatId reached Telegram) or strengthen it by re-fetching from botRepository.findById(seeded.getId()).block() and asserting on the reloaded document if the round-trip is what's intended.

findings.issue: Redundant existing.setOwnerChatId(null) after seedConnectedBot — the helper never sets ownerChatId, so the field is already null by default. The explicit set documents intent but is otherwise no-op.
findings.suggestion: Optional: keep for self-documentation (the next reader scanning for the null branch sees the contract spelled out), or drop and rely on the default. Either is fine; flagged only because the codebase elsewhere relies on field defaults without explicit nulling.
